about: Shared cases for the move-forward plan screen. tamarket/moveon.py (screen_plan) passes all of them; a port must too. Each case starts from base_plan and base_household, then applies, in this order: delete (dotted paths), set (dotted path to value; a number in a path is a list index), set_parts (dotted path to a list of strings joined with nothing between them) and household_set (fields of the record); review, when given, is the list of usable reviewer notes passed to the screen. expect gives passed and the sorted set of rules among the problems. Strings that would trip the repository's own screen are stored as parts, as fd-core's own tests do. The deny list is not used here: pages never receive it.

base_household.record_type: synthetic household, not a real person

summary.text: A household of 3 in nightly-paid, self-contained accommodation for 57 weeks, placed outside the district, with one support need. Social housing and a private rented sector offer could both be considered, and supported housing could be an option if the household wants it.

pathway_suggestions.why: If the household is owed the main housing duty, the allocation scheme must give it reasonable preference (s.166A(3)(b)).
A private rented sector offer could end the main housing duty if the household accepts or refuses it and the conditions in s.193(7AA) are met.
The record lists a history of mental health problems, and supported housing could give support alongside a home.

steps.text: Confirm which duty the household is owed and record it.
Ask the household what it wants before any referral or offer.
Check the children's schooling and the support the household uses before any move out of the current area.

officer_checks.text: Check that any offer is suitable for the household, including space, location and affordability (s.193(7F); Code chapter 17).
Check each condition in article 3 of the 2012 Order before approving the offer (Code 17.15 and 17.16).
Check that written notice went to the council where the accommodation is within 14 days (s.208(2) to (4)).

risks.text: A move could disrupt the children's school and the support the household uses.
A private tenancy could cost more than the household can afford once support ends.
